targetText: All the experience of the ten months of war proves the error both of the theory of China's inevitable subjugation and of the theory of China's quick victory. The former gives rise to the tendency to compromise and the latter to the tendency to underestimate the enemy. Both approaches to the problem are subjective and one-sided, or, in a word, unscientific.
summary: Both the belief that China is doomed to lose and the belief that China will win quickly are unscientific errors that focus on only one side of reality.
explanation: Mao applies materialist dialectics to critique two opposite forms of subjectivism: capitulationist pessimism, which sees only Japan's military strength, and rash optimism, which ignores China's material weaknesses after isolated tactical victories.
context: In any long liberation or labor struggle, exaggerating the opponent's power leads to surrender, while underestimating their resources after a single win leads to reckless defeat.
